stem.en: A horse pulls a cart. By the third law, the cart pulls the horse back with an equal force. Why do these two forces not cancel each other?

text.en: The horse pulls a little harder than the cart pulls back.

feedback.en: By the third law, the two forces are always equal. They do not cancel for a different reason.

text.en: The third law works only for objects at rest.

feedback.en: The third law holds for moving objects too.

text.en: The two forces act on different objects: one on the cart, one on the horse.

feedback.en: Right. Forces cancel only when they act on the same object.

explanation.en: The two forces of a third-law pair act on different objects, so they never cancel. To see whether the cart speeds up, add only the forces on the cart: the pull of the horse forwards and friction backwards.

hints.en: Which object does each force act on?
